name: Gaza Biennale
known: Hyperallergic describes the museum, also called the Forbidden Museum, as a Palestinian cultural institution "without walls" in the occupied West Bank, co-founded by Fidaa Ataya and the visual artist Andreas Ibrahim and inaugurated by the Palestinian Ministry of Culture at the summit of Al Risan moun
The Istanbul pavilion, "A Cloud in My Hand", ran at Depo from 19 September to 8 November 2025 during the 18th International Istanbul Biennale, curated by House of Taswir.

name: The Freedom Theatre
known: Director Ahmed Tobasi was held about 14 hours and released, and Ismael Hussam Ibrahim, 25, was arrested and freed the next day (Al Jazeera, Mauricio Morales, 20 December 2023).

The Jewish Chronicle (partisan) states that the British Council is funded by the Foreign Office and that the theatre backs the BDS movement, and says founder Zakaria Zubeidi led the al-Aqsa Martyrs Brigades.
Conservative MP Robert Halfon called the funding "pretty shocking" and urged the government to act on its pledge to stop publicly funded bodies supporting BDS.
Staff told Al Jazeera that Israeli forces raided it in December 2023 and arrested two directors.
Co-founder Juliano Mer-Khamis was shot dead in 2011.

name: Al Ma'mal Foundation for Contemporary Art
known: Founded in 1998 by Jack Persekian, an artist and curator, after his Anadiel Gallery (opened in the early 1990s on Salah al-Din Street, moved to the Old City in 1996) and its circle decided to open a contemporary art foundation (Jerusalem Story, 12 September 2024).
Persekian is named as director in Gulf News (2018).
The Jerusalem Story piece lists Shireen Mufdi as deputy director.
Names its board of directors and General Assembly.

name: A.M. Qattan Foundation
known: His son Omar Al-Qattan chairs it (The Art Newspaper, 25 June 2018;

name: Khalil Sakakini Cultural Center
known: Directors: Adila Laïdi-Hanieh was the first director (1996 to 2005, per Wikipedia).

name: Riwaq Biennale
known: Art biennale run by Riwaq, the Centre for Architectural Conservation, a non-governmental, non-profit organisation in Ramallah that protects Palestinian cultural heritage (e-flux, OPEC Fund project page).

Riwaq's director Khaldun Bshara writes that the biennale gave Riwaq exposure beyond the heritage world and "opened new funding possibilities", and that there was no fourth edition in 2011 after resistance within Riwaq (PARSE Journal, Khaldun Bshara).

The third edition, "A Geography: 50 Villages", ran in Palestine from June to October 2009 and was curated by Reem Fadda and Charles Esche as tours, curated conversations and temporary interventions (Bidoun, Beth Stryker).

name: Biomuseo
known: The executive director is Victor Cucalón Imbert and the board president is Liza Henríquez (stated by the space).

name: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Panamá
known: Founded by the Instituto Panameño de Arte (Panarte) in 1962 and host venue of the Panama Art Biennials.

name: Papua New Guinea National Museum and Art Gallery
known: Directors named by Wikipedia include Soroi Eoe from 1985 to 2005 and Andrew Moutu from 2011 to 2016 and again from 2018 to 2022.

On 11 September 2015 Prime Minister Tony Abbott announced US$17.5 million over four years to upgrade the museum, to mark the 40th anniversary of PNG's independence (RNZ, "PNG Museum funding announced by Australia", republished by the Council of Australasian Museum Directors).

name: Centro Cultural de la República El Cabildo
known: Margarita Morselli was director general (ABC Color, 2019).
Its director Saucedo Rodas said in July 2024 that its budget was 31,000 million guaraníes, shared with the Congress's Central Library and Archive (La Nación, 12 July 2024).

name: Museo del Barro
known: La Nación reported on 25 November 2023 that the museum and the Fundación Itaú invited the public to the opening of "Arte para (imaginar) un país", curated by Ticio Escobar and Osvaldo Salerno.

name: Lugar de la Memoria, la Tolerancia y la Inclusión Social (LUM)
known: It is one of the 56 museums run by the Culture Ministry's General Directorate of Museums (LUM Memoria 2023).
The Culture Ministry removed director Manuel Burga in January 2025 without explanation and barred a Palestinian film in October 2026.

name: MAC Lima
known: The Spanish Wikipedia infobox lists Pedro Pablo Alayza as director and Eduardo Hochschild Beeck as president.

name: Museo Larco
known: Its formal name, Museo Arqueológico Rafael Larco Herrera, honours the founder's father.
Andrés Álvarez Calderón Larco is president and chief executive and Ulla Holmquist Pachas is director (stated by the museum).
Andina (7 November 2017) quoted him as director.
The collection began with the holdings of the founder's father, Rafael Larco Herrera, which Larco Hoyle expanded by buying large lots from other collectors (Wikipedia).
Its directory names only an executive president and a director, not a board.
Led by president and CEO Andrés Álvarez Calderón Larco.

name: Museo de Arte de Lima
known: Alberto Rebaza chairs the board.

name: Pinto Art Museum
known: Unverified: the museum takes a 50 percent commission on artworks it sells, according to former curator Riel Jaramillo Hilario, quoted in Lifestyle Asia (9 April 2021).
He is a named former curator; the article says the museum had issued no official statement.
It names only its founder, Dr.
